text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has called on all party members and officials to help improve the lives of ethnic minority people to draw them into the nation-building process.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam visited Morocco on Sunday to improve political and economic ties between the two countries.
-- Vietnam's cumulative trade deficit in the first 11 months of this year was $3.71 billion, with exports at $6.47 billion and imports at $10.18 billion.

-- The United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) will provide $500,000 to help a refrigeration and engineering enterprise in Danang and a sea product refrigeration company in Ho Chi Minh City adopt environmentally friendly processes.
-- A delegation from the Chinese Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries arrived in Ho Chi Minh City for a five-day visit.
-- Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and NEC Corp and Hong Kong's PHS International Ltd have launched trials of the personal handyphone system in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam will auction 50 billion dong ($4.48 million) worth of six-month Treasury bills on Wednesday.
-- The Transport Ministry will invest 17.5 billion dong ($1.6 million) to upgrade the highway linking the northern mountainous provinces of Tuyen Quang, Yen Bai, Lai Chau and Hanoi.

-- The Standing Board of the Communist Party's Politburo has issued instructions on heightening the role of the state economic sector and reinforcing state management and control over foreign trade and the trade activities of all the economic sectors.
-- Some 2.1 tonnes of gold was imported to Ho Chi Minh City in the first 11 month of this year.
-- The price of coffee plantation areas in the central highland province of Dak Lak has dropped sharply following the fall of coffee prices in recent months.
